rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He quotes 47:17, where God increases the guidance of those already guided.
rows.anchor: والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى [محمد: 17]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that guidance comes through reinforcing proofs, resolving doubts, and casting insights.
rows.anchor: والثالث: بتوكيد الأدلة وحل الشبهة وإلقاء الخواطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being on light means being upon a proof and guidance from one's Lord.
rows.anchor: { فهو على نور } أي على دلالة وهدى

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says proofs are called light because they reveal truth as light reveals worldly things.
rows.anchor: شبه الأدلة بالنور لأن بها يعرف الحق كما بالنور تعرف أمور الدنيا عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the light as God's Book, which is the source one follows and returns to.
rows.anchor: وقيل: النور كتاب الله عز وجل فبه نأخذ وإليه ننتهي عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with the hard-hearted person is omitted; the following warning identifies the missing counterpart.
rows.anchor: وحذف كمن هو قاسي القلب يدل على المحذوف

words: فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلْقَٰسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُم مِّن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hard-hearted are habituated to disbelief and stubbornly attached to it; preaching, inducement, threats, and Quran recitation do not soften them.
rows.anchor: وهم الذين ألفوا الكفر وتعصبوا له وتصلبت قلوبهم حتى لا ينجع فيها وعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their manifest error means they have turned away from the truth in an obvious way.
rows.anchor: أي عدول عن الحق { مبين } أي ظاهر واضح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best discourse is the Quran; it is called hadith as God's speech, like the Prophet's speech, and as revelation later than earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: { الله نزل أحسن الحديث } يعني القرآن سماه الله حديثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is best for its extreme eloquence, inimitability, and inclusion of needed proofs, law, exhortation, prophetic stories, promise, and warning.
rows.anchor: وهو أحسن الحديث لفرط فصاحته ولإعجازه واشتماله على جميع ما يحتاج المكلف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its passages resemble and confirm one another, with no disagreement or contradiction.
rows.anchor: { كتابا متشابها } يشبه بعضه بعضا ويصدق بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says the Quran resembles earlier revealed books while being more comprehensive and beneficial.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه يشبه كتب الله المتقدمة وإن كان أعم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes its resemblance to mean consistency in fine composition, strong diction, and excellent meanings.
rows.anchor: وقيل: متشابها في حسن النظم وجزالة اللفظ وجودة المعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called mathani because stories, reports, rulings, and exhortations recur in varied forms of expression.
rows.anchor: { مثاني } سمي بذلك لأنه يثنى فيه بعض القصص والأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its repeated recitation does not become tiresome because of the beauty of its sound.
rows.anchor: ويثنى أيضا في التلاوة فلا يمل لحسن مسموعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Skin shivers at Quranic threats, then softens at promises of reward and mercy; hearts settle with God's mention of Paradise and reward, whose object is omitted.
rows.anchor: { تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم } أي تأخذهم قشعريرة خوفا مما في القرآن من الوعيد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that when a servant's skin shivers from fear of God, sins fall away like leaves from a dry tree.
rows.anchor: إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله تحاتت عنه ذنوبه كما يتحات عن الشجرة اليابسة ورقها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda describes God's friends as shivering and then finding calm in remembrance; loss of reason and fainting belong to innovators and come from Satan.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: هذا نعت لأولياء الله نعتهم بأن تقشعر جلودهم وتطمئن قلوبهم إلى ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That guidance refers to the Quran.
rows.anchor: ذلك } يعني القرآن { هدى الله

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says God guides by the Quran's proofs those of Muhammad's community to whom He gave it.
rows.anchor: من عباده بما نصب فيه من الأدلة وهم الذين آتاهم القرآن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says those who benefit from guidance are singled out as guided because those who fail to follow it cannot be described as guided.
rows.anchor: إنما خصهم بذلك لأنهم المنتفعون بالهداية ومن لم يهتد لا يوصف

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī explains misguidance as being turned from the path to Paradise, with no one able to guide the person there.
rows.anchor: ومن يضلل الله } عن طريق الجنة { فما له من هاد

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim explains the phrase as straying away from God and His mercy, with no guide remaining.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه من ضل عن الله ورحمته فلا هادي له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation is deprivation of increases in guidance and grace, since the unbeliever has no such grace.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه من يضلله عن زيادة الهدى والألطاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question contrasts one who wards off punishment with his face on Judgment Day and one who comes safe from the Fire; the face is named because it is a person's most honored part.
rows.anchor: تقديره أفحال من يدفع عذاب الله بوجهه يوم القيامة كحال من يأتي منا لا تمسه النار

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says this is the person thrown into Hell face-first, so the face is the first part touched by the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أمن يلقى في النار منكوسا فأول عضو منه مسته النار وجهه عن عطاء

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: The verb means to shield oneself; ʿAntara's line describes people advancing him to battle to protect themselves from the spears' heat.
rows.anchor: عنترة: إذ يتقون بي الأسنة لم أخم عنها ولكني تضايق مقدمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers of Hell tell the wrongdoers to taste the recompense for the sins they committed.
rows.anchor: أي جزاء ما كسبتموه من المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples rejected God's signs and denied His messengers, then punishment seized them suddenly while they felt safe and unaware.
rows.anchor: بآيات الله وجحدوا رسله { فأتاهم العذاب } عاجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chest-opening question follows the earlier proofs of divine unity and justice: reflection on them opens the heart and settles certainty.
rows.anchor: إنما اتصل قوله { أفمن شرح الله صدره }

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim links the Quran as the best discourse to the prior command to follow the best saying, making the Quran especially worthy of following.
rows.anchor: واتصل قوله { الله نزل أحسن الحديث } بما تقدمه من قوله { فبشر عبادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows by implying that one who has not followed God's guidance cannot find guidance elsewhere; the face-shielding person remains in disbelief.
rows.anchor: اتصل قوله { أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب } بما قبله

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: The Kufan readers except ʿĀṣim, together with Abū Jaʿfar, read the plural عباده; the remaining readers read the singular عبده.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم وأبو جعفر بكاف عباده على الجمع والباقون عبده على التوحيد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains the singular reading with the following clause: God is sufficient for you while they frighten you.
rows.anchor: حجة من قرأ عبده ويخوفونك فكأن المعنى ليس الله بكافيك

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains the plural as God sufficing His prophets, as He protected Abraham from fire, Noah from drowning, and Jonah from his plight, and so will suffice Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ عباده فالمعنى أليس الله بكاف عباده الأنبياء كما كفى إبراهيم النار

rows.speaker: أهل البصرة
rows.claim: Readers of Basra pronounce tanwin on كاشفات and ممسكات and put the following nouns in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل البصرة كاشفات وممسكات بالتنوين وما بعدهما منصوبان

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers omit tanwin and use genitive annexation to the following nouns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بغير تنوين على إضافة كل واحدة منهما إلى ما بعدها

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says accusative fits an unfulfilled or present participle; genitive follows omission of tanwin, with annexation replacing it although the sense retains tanwin.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ كاشفات ضره وممسكات رحمته فالوجه فيه أنه مما لم يقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After promising the truthful and those who affirm truth, God assures them He will suffice them despite enemies who target and harm them; here the servant is Muhammad.
rows.anchor: لما وعد الله سبحانه الصادق والمصدق عقبه بأنه يكفيهم وإن كانت الأعداء تقصدهم وتؤذيهم

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Suddī, and Ibn Zayd say the unbelievers frightened Muhammad with the idols they worshipped, claiming their gods would destroy him.
rows.anchor: كانت الكفار تخوفه بالأوثان التي كانوا يعبدونها عن قتادة والسدي وابن زيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative report says that when Khālid went to break al-ʿUzzā on the Prophet's order, people warned him of the idol's might; he struck it and declared God had humiliated it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه لما قصد خالد لكسر العزى بأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One whom God misguides through disbelief and sins from the path to Paradise has no guide who can lead him there.
rows.anchor: أي من أضله الله عن طريق الجنة بكفره ومعاصيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation means that once a person has strayed from truth, no one can call that person a guide.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أن من وصفه بأنه ضال إذ ضل هو عن الحق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation is that God withholds increases in guidance from the person, leaving no one to provide that increase.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من يحرمه الله من زيادات الهدى فليس له زائد

words: وَمَن يَهْدِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّضِلٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever God guides toward Paradise cannot be led away from it by anyone.
rows.anchor: أي من يهده الله إلى طريق الجنة فلا أحد يضله عنها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One alternative says that once a person is guided and rightly follows, no one can turn that person aside.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من يهده الله فاهتدى فلا يقدر أحد على صرفه عنه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative says that whoever merits increased guidance has risen beyond the influence of whispering.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من بلغ استحقاق زيادات الهدى فقد ارتفع عن تأثير الوسواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty, able, and overpowering, with retribution against enemies who deny His favors.
rows.anchor: أي قادر قاهر لا يقدر أحد على مغالبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even while worshipping idols, the unbelievers acknowledge that God created the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: الفاعل لذلك لأنهم مع عبادتهم الأوثان يقرون بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot remove harm or withhold mercy; beings powerless to benefit or harm cannot rightly be worshipped, unlike God, who has power over all and cannot be thwarted.
rows.anchor: أن من عجز عن النفع والضر وكشف السوء والشر عمن يتقرب إليه كيف يحسن منه عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After people ignore the proofs and exhortations, God commands Muhammad to ask Him to judge them as they deserve.
rows.anchor: لما قدم سبحانه ذكر الأدلة فلم ينظروا فيها والمواعظ فلم يتعظوا بها أمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāṭir means creator and originator of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: { اللهم فاطر السماوات والأرض } أي يا خالقهما ومنشئهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what is hidden from all creatures as well as what they witness and know.
rows.anchor: أي يا عالم ما غاب علمه عن جميع الخلق وعالم ما شهدوه وعلموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day God resolves the worldly religious and worldly disputes among His servants, deciding rights and wrongs; Muhammad asks for a just judgment between him and his people.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة { فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون } في دار الدنيا من أمر دينهم ودنياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supplication promises believers victory, since God commanded it in order to answer it.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا بشارة للمؤمنين بالظفر والنصر لأنه سبحانه إنما أمره به للإجابة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says he knows a verse that no one recites and then asks God for something without receiving it: this supplication.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب أنه قال: إني لأعرف موضع آية

words: مَا فِي ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا وَمِثْلَهُۥ مَعَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even possessing everything on earth and as much again would not save the wrongdoers from punishment; they would offer it as ransom.
rows.anchor: { ولو أن للذين ظلموا ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day forms of punishment they never expected or thought would reach them become visible.
rows.anchor: أي ظهر لهم يوم القيامة من صنوف العذاب ما لم يكونوا ينتظرونه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says they had thought their deeds were good, but now those deeds appeared as evil.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: ظنوا أعمالهم حسنات فبدت لهم سيئات

rows.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munkadir became distressed at death because he feared God might reveal something he had not reckoned with.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن محمد بن المنكدر جزع عند الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil consequences of their deeds also appear to them.
rows.anchor: أي جزاء سيئات أعمالهم { وحاق بهم } أي نزل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warnings of punishment that the Prophet gave, which they denied and mocked, now befall them.
rows.anchor: وهو كل ما ينذرهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مما كانوا ينكرونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When illness or distress touches a person, he calls sincerely as a Muslim, knowing only God can remove it.
rows.anchor: من مرض أو شدة { دعانا } واستغاث بنا مسلما مخلصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's granting a favor means giving health, bodily well-being, abundant livelihood, or another blessing.
rows.anchor: أي أعطيناه نعمة من الصحة في الجسم والسعة في الرزق

rows.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Jubbāʾī say the speaker claims he obtained the blessing through his own knowledge, effort, and skill, exposing ignorance about the sources of benefit and harm.
rows.anchor: قال إنما أوتيته بعلمي وجلدي وحيلتي عن الحسن والجبائي

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatāda and Muqātil explain the claim as a report of knowledge God knew the person possessed.
rows.anchor: على علم على خبر علمه الله عندي عن قتادة ومقاتل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the speaker thinks the blessing came because God approves of him.
rows.anchor: وثالثها: على علم يرضاه عني فلذلك أتاني ما أتاني من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing is a trial that reveals whether the recipient is grateful or patient, with recompense according to the response.
rows.anchor: أي بلية واختبار يبتليه الله بها فيظهر كيف شكره أو صبره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says the blessing itself becomes punishment when they attribute it to themselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه هذه النعمة فتنة أي عذاب لهم إذا أضافوها إلى أنفسهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative takes the boastful statement itself as their trial, because they will be punished for saying it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه هذه المقالة التي قالوها فتنة لهم لأنهم يعاقبون عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most do not distinguish affliction from blessing.
rows.anchor: } البلوى من النعمى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they do not know all blessings come from God, even when acquired through human causes.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يعلمون أن النعم كلها من الله وإن حصلت بأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People before them made the same boast; Qarun is an example, saying he received his wealth through knowledge of his own.
rows.anchor: أي قد قال مثل هذه الكلمة وهذه المقالة

words: فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their amassed wealth did not help them and instead became a burden against them.
rows.anchor: أي فلم ينفعهم ما كانوا يجمعونه من الأموال بل صارت وبالا عليهم

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The readers of Medina and Abū ʿAmr read وأن يظهر with a causative verb and الفساد in the accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وأن يظهر بغير ألف قبل الواو ويظهر بضم الياء وكسر الهاء الفساد بالنصب

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read وإن يظهر with يظهر opened and الفساد nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر وإن يظهر بفتح الياء الفساد بالرفع

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: حفص ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ and Yaʿqūb read أو أن يظهر with ḍamma on yāʾ and accusative الفساد.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص ويعقوب أو أن يظهر بضم الياء الفساد بالنصب

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers read أو أن يظهر with fatḥa on yāʾ and nominative الفساد.
rows.anchor: والباقون أو أن يظهر بفتح الياء الفساد بالرفع

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains أو أن as one kind of feared action, like saying eat bread or dates, whereas وإن makes two separate things feared.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: من قرأ أو أن يظهر فالمعنى إني أخاف هذا الضرب منه

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the causative reading makes Moses the agent, parallel to the preceding threat to change their religion; the intransitive reading makes corruption appear in the land.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ يظهر في الأرض الفساد فأسند الفعل إلى موسى

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم وأبو عمرو وإسماعيل عن نافع وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers assimilate the ذ of عذت into ت, as also in فنبذتها; the remaining readers pronounce it distinctly.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم وأبو عمرو وإسماعيل عن نافع وأبو جعفر عذت هنا وفي الدخان بإدغام الذال في التاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says assimilation is good because the letters are close; distinct pronunciation is also good since their articulation groups differ, though all are produced near the tongue tip and incisors.
rows.anchor: فأما الإدغام في عذت فحسن لتقارب الحرفين والإظهار حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh tells his people to leave him to kill Moses, implying that some of his intimates had urged him not to do so and feared Moses might pray and destroy him.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه كان في خاصة فرعون قوم يشيرون عليه بأن لا يقتل موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh means they should tell Moses to call on his Lord for help in escaping death, since Pharaoh arrogantly claims the prayer will do nothing.
rows.anchor: معناه وقولوا له ليدع ربه وليستعن به في دفع القتل عنه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says Pharaoh's people called Moses a sorcerer and feared killing him before proof appeared would strengthen suspicion, so they proposed delaying and summoning the magicians.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم قالوا له هو ساحر فإن قتلته قبل ظهور الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh fears Moses will change the religion of his people, meaning their belief in Pharaoh's gods.
rows.anchor: إن لم أقتله وهو ما تعتقدونه من إلهتي

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claims Moses may gain followers and provoke fighting that devastates the land and brings disorder.
rows.anchor: بأن يتبعه قوم ويحتاج إلى أن نقاتله فيخرب فيما بين ذلك البلاد ويظهر الفساد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Pharaoh considered obedience to God to be corruption.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الفساد عند فرعون أن يعمل بطاعة الله عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses takes refuge in his and Pharaoh's Creator against every arrogant person who refuses to believe in Judgment Day, asking God to repel that person's harm.
rows.anchor: أي إني اعتصمت بربي الذي خلقني وربكم الذي خلقكم من شر كل متكبر

words: رَجُلٌۭ مُّؤْمِنٌۭ مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَٰنَهُۥ
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh says dissimulation is part of his and his forefathers' religion, and one who has no dissimulation has no religion.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله ع: التقية من ديني ودين آبائي ولا دين لمن لا تقية له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dissimulation is God's shield on earth, because the believing man from Pharaoh's family would have been killed had he openly declared Islam.
rows.anchor: والتقية ترس الله في الأرض لأن مؤمن آل فرعون لو أظهر الإسلام لقتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the only other believers in Pharaoh's family were Pharaoh's wife and the believer who warned Moses that the council planned to kill him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يكن من آل فرعون مؤمن غيره وغير امرأة فرعون

rows.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and Muqātil say he was Pharaoh's cousin who believed in Moses and was the man who came running from the farthest part of the city.
rows.anchor: قال السدي ومقاتل كان ابن عم فرعون وكان آمن بموسى وهو الذي جاء من أقصى المدينة يسعى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says he was Pharaoh's designated successor and was named Ḥabīb.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه كان ولي عهده من بعده وكان اسمه حبيب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A separate report gives his name as Ḥizbīl.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اسمه حزبيل

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes them; using a participle meaning a man who says my Lord is God would not show that belief is the reason for killing him.
rows.anchor: وهو استفهام إنكار ولو قال أتقتلون رجلا قائلا ربي الله لم يدل على أن القتل من أجل الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subjunctive أن يقول is a causal object, meaning they would kill him because he says that his Lord is God.
rows.anchor: فموضع أن يقول نصب على أنه مفعول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proofs of Moses' truth include the staff, the hand, and other miracles.
rows.anchor: أي بما يدل على صدقه من المعجزات مثل العصا واليد وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer softens his argument by saying that if Moses lies, the consequence falls on him, like the diplomatic wording in 34:24.
rows.anchor: إنما قال هذا على وجه التلطف كقوله

words: وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًۭا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says Moses promised rescue for belief and destruction for disbelief; whichever course they chose, one of his promised outcomes would reach them.
rows.anchor: قيل: إن موسى كان يعدهم بالنجاة إن آمنوا وبالهلاك إن كفروا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says his warnings included different events, such as destruction in this world and punishment in the next; earthly destruction is part of the warning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال { بعض الذي يعدكم } لأنه توعدهم أمورا مختلفة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some can idiomatically mean all as a tactful or expansive expression; the cited poem says the patient may attain some of his wish while the hasty may err.
rows.anchor: وقيل: استعمل البعض في موضع الكل تلطفا في الخطاب وتوسعا في الكلام كما قال الشاعر: قد يدرك

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā says the believer argues that even part of Moses' warning suffices to destroy them, so the whole warning is more than enough.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى: إنما قال بعض الذي يعدكم على المظاهرة بالحجاج أي أنه يكفي بعضه

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement means God does not guide to Paradise and reward someone excessive in sin and lying about God.
rows.anchor: أي لا يهدي إلى جنته وثوابه من هو مسرف على نفسه متجاوز عن الحد في المعصية

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence may continue the believer's words, or it may begin a new statement from God.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون هذا حكاية عن قول المؤمن ويجوز أن يكون ابتداء الكلام من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer reminds them that they now rule over the people of the earth, meaning they hold power over Egypt.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكرهم هذا المؤمن ما هم فيه من الملك ليشكروا الله على ذلك بالإيمان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are dominant, prevailing over the land and subduing its people.
rows.anchor: أي عالين فيها غالبين عليها قاهرين لأهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer warns them not to bring God's punishment upon themselves by killing the Prophet and denying him, since no one can prevent it.
rows.anchor: ومعناه لا تتعرضوا لعذاب الله بقتل النبي وتكذيبه فلا مانع لعذاب من عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recalls the people of Hell disputing: leaders and followers quarrel, with the weak followers addressing those who had been arrogant.
rows.anchor: معناه واذكر يا محمد لقومك الوقت الذي يحتاج فيه أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak are the followers, and those who acted arrogantly are their leaders.
rows.anchor: فيقول الضعفاء } وهم الأتباع { للذين استكبروا } وهم الرؤساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The followers say they obeyed the leaders and answered their calls.
rows.anchor: وكنا نمتثل أمركم ونجيبكم إلى ما تدعوننا إليه

words: فَهَلْ أَنتُم مُّغْنُونَ عَنَّا نَصِيبًۭا مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask whether the leaders can carry away a share of their torment, since a leader is responsible for protecting followers who obey him.
rows.anchor: لأنه يلزم الرئيس الدفع عن أتباعه والمنقادين لأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders answer that they and their followers are all in Hell together.
rows.anchor: أي نحن وأنتم في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may parse كل as a subject with two predicates, or as the predicate of إنّا, meaning all are together in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وكل فيها مبتدأ وخبر في موضع رفع بأنه خبران ويجوز أن يكون كل خبر أن

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ حَكَمَ بَيْنَ ٱلْعِبَادِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has decreed that no one bears another's punishment and that He will surely punish those who associate another with Him in worship.
rows.anchor: بأن لا يتحمل أحد عن أحد وأنه يعاقب من أشرك به وعبد معه غيره لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guards of Hell are the angels assigned to administer punishment to its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وهم الذين يتولون عذاب أهل النار من الملائكة الموكلين بهم

words: ٱدْعُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ يُخَفِّفْ عَنَّا يَوْمًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unable to endure severe torment, they beg for one day's relief, still hoping despite knowing by necessary knowledge that punishment never ends or lessens.
rows.anchor: يقولون ذلك لأنه لا طاقة لهم على شدة العذاب ولشدة جزعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the question, the omitted subject of كان is القصة, and the following clause about messengers explains that story.
rows.anchor: التقدير أو لم تك القصة وتأتيكم رسلكم تفسير القصة فاسم كان مضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guards ask whether messengers had brought clear proofs of divine unity and prophethood, since the sinners disbelieved and stubbornly resisted.
rows.anchor: أي الحجج والدلالات على صحة التوحيد والنبوات أي فكفرتم وعاندتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people admit that messengers and proofs came, but say they denied them and rejected the messengers' prophethood.
rows.anchor: جاءتنا الرسل والبينات فكذبناهم وجحدنا نبوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guards tell the inhabitants to pray for themselves because the guards may pray only with permission and have not received it.
rows.anchor: أي قالت الخزنة فادعوا أنتم فإنا لا ندعوا إلا بإذن ولم يؤذن لنا فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One alternative takes the guards' words as contemptuous dismissal.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما قالوا ذلك استخفافا بهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative says the guards tell them to pray for woe and destruction.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه فادعوا بالويل والثبور

words: وَمَا دُعَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers' supplication is futile because it brings them no benefit.
rows.anchor: أي في ضياع لأنه لا ينتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabiʿ can be a verbal noun or a plural of tābiʿ, comparable to other singular and plural pairs.
rows.anchor: التبع يصلح أن يكون مصدرا يقال تبع تبعا ويجوز أن يكون جمع تابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭawʿan and karhan are verbal nouns used as circumstantial accusatives, meaning obediently or reluctantly; ṭāʾiʿīn is also a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: طوعا وكرها مصدران وضعا موضع الحال التقدير ائتيا تطيعان إطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase seven heavens is likewise an accusative circumstantial expression after the action is completed.
rows.anchor: سبع سماوات أيضا منصوب على الحال بعد الفراغ من الفعل

words: ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَهِىَ دُخَانٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God then directed Himself to creating the heaven, which was smoke.
rows.anchor: أي ثم قصد إلى خلق السماء وكانت السماء دخانا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the smoke was vapor from the earth.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كانت بخار الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basic sense of istiwāʾ is straightness and direction toward arranging matters properly.
rows.anchor: وأصل الاستواء الاستقامة والقصد للتدبير المستقيم تسوية له

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan offers the alternative that God's command turned toward the heaven.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ثم استوى أمره إلى السماء عن الحسن

words: فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًۭا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the heaven came with the sun, moon, and stars, while the earth came with its rivers, trees, and fruits.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أتت السماء بما فيها من الشمس والقمر والنجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command and reply are not literal speech: God reports creating heaven and earth without difficulty, as though an order were instantly obeyed.
rows.anchor: ليس هناك أمر بالقول على الحقيقة ولا جواب لذلك القول بل أخبر الله سبحانه عن اختراعه السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation-without-delay image is like God's command that when He wills something, He says Be, and it is.
rows.anchor: إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub says the masculine plural means the heavens and earth came bringing the rational beings within them, whose grammatical gender prevails.
rows.anchor: لأن المعنى أتينا بمن فينا من العقلاء فغلب حكم العقلاء عن قطرب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says they were addressed as rational speakers, so the reply uses the rational plural, as in 21:33.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه لما خوطبن خطاب من يعقل جمعن جمع من يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poetic example has an animal addressed with humanlike perception and praise, illustrating speech that treats a nonhuman as rational.
rows.anchor: قال: فأجهشت للبوباة حين رأيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second anonymous poem addresses a ruin as if it could speak, another example of attributing rational speech to something nonhuman.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر: ألا أنعم صباحا أيها الرسم وانطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This wording indicates that heaven was created after earth and that earth's provisions were created before it was spread out.
rows.anchor: يفيد أنه خلق السماء بعد الأرض وخلق الأقوات فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later statement that earth was spread after that is reconciled by saying earth already existed but was not spread until after heaven was created.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فتكون الفائدة فيه أن الأرض كانت مخلوقة غير مدحوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first made heaven smoke, then layered it into seven heavens and adorned it with lamps to show His intrinsic power, knowledge, and independence while all else depends on Him.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل الله السماء أولا دخانا ثم سماوات أطباقا ثم زينها بالمصابيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He completed, perfected, and finished making the seven heavens.
rows.anchor: أي صنعهن وأحكمهن وفرغ من خلقهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two days were Thursday and Friday.
rows.anchor: { سبع سماوات في يومين } يوم الخميس والجمعة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says Friday was named because the creation of heaven and earth was gathered together on that day.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: إنما سمي جمعة لأنه جمع فيه خلق السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: السدي وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and Qatāda say God created in each heaven what He willed, including angels and other things.
rows.anchor: أي خلق فيها ما أراده من ملك وغيره عن السدي وقتادة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil instead explains that God commanded each heaven to carry out what He willed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وأمر في كل سماء بما أراد عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazgh is a prod or sting that incites wrongdoing, as if poking someone toward conduct contrary to sound judgment.
rows.anchor: النزغ النخس بما يدعو إلى الفساد يقال نزغ ينزغ فلان ينزغ فلانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥād means turning away from truth; laḥada is also used with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وألحد: مال عن الحق ويقال لحد يلحد أيضا بمعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is called remembrance because it contains proofs and rulings.
rows.anchor: ويسمى القرآن ذكرا لأنه ذكر فيه الدلائل والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إمّا is إن of condition with ما added for emphasis; this resembles an oath and therefore takes the emphatic nūn on the verb.
rows.anchor: وإما ينزغنك هي إن التي للجزاء زيد عليها ما تأكيدا فأشبه لذلك القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause leaves the predicate of إن الذين كفروا implicit, understood as they will be punished.
rows.anchor: إن الذين كفروا بالذكر لم يذكر لأن خبرا والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, أولئك ينادون من مكان بعيد can serve as the predicate of the clause.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الخبر أولئك ينادون من مكان بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Satan's prompting diverts the Prophet from forbearance, he is told to seek God's protection from Satan's harm.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يستعيذ بالله إذا صرفه الشيطان عن الاحتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of this clause is given at the end of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: الآية مفسرة في آخر سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are proofs of God's oneness and signs of attributes by which He differs from all creatures.
rows.anchor: أي حججه الدالة على وحدانيته وأدلته على صفاته التي باين بها جميع خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is the sun's departure from the earth's surface, and day its rising over it; both follow stable measures and an enduring order.
rows.anchor: { الليل } بذهاب الشمس عن بسيط الأرض { والنهار } بطلوعها على وجهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon have distinctive lights and display ordered motion in their courses.
rows.anchor: وما اختصا به من النور وظهر فيهما من التدبير في المسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite their many benefits, the sun and moon are not creators and must not be worshipped.
rows.anchor: وإن كان فيهما منافع كثيرة لأنهما ليسا بخالقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine plural pronoun can refer to a nonrational plural, which may take feminine singular or plural agreement, as in his example about sheep.
rows.anchor: أن ضمير غير ما يعقل على لفظ التأنيث تقول هذا كباشك فسقها وإن شئت قلت فسقهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the meaning of آيات, since the verse introduces these objects as God's signs.
rows.anchor: والآخر: أن الضمير يرجع إلى معنى الآيات لأنه قال ومن آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they truly intend to worship God, they must prostrate to Him alone and no other.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم تقصدون بعبادتكم الله كما تزعمون الله فاسجدوا لله دون غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people refuse exclusive worship, the angels near God glorify Him night and day without tiring.
rows.anchor: وهم الملائكة { يسبحون له بالليل والنهار وهم لا يسأمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of the angels' tireless worship is given in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: وهو مفسر في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن المسيب
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and Ibn al-Musayyib place the prostration-of-recitation at the end of verse 38, after وهم لا يسأمون.
rows.anchor: والمروي عن ابن عباس وقتادة وابن المسيب أن موضع السجود عند قوله { وهم لا يسأمون }

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan place the prostration-of-recitation after إن كنتم إياه تعبدون; Abū ʿAmr chooses this placement, also reported from the Imams.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود والحسن أنه عند قوله { إن كنتم إياه تعبدون } وهو اختيار أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī explain the humbled earth as dusty, worn out, and broken down.
rows.anchor: أي غبراء دارسة متهشمة عن قتادة والسدي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation calls it dead and dry with no vegetation; al-Azharī says dry earth without rain is described as humbled.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ميتة يابسة لا نبات فيها قال الأزهري إذا يبست الأرض ولم تمطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When water falls, the earth stirs with vegetation, swells, and rises before the plants sprout.
rows.anchor: أي تحركت بالنبات وربت أي انتفخت وارتفعت قبل أن تنبت
